name: Auditory Neuropathy Spectrum Disorder

criteria.description: Presence of normal otoacoustic emissions indicating intact outer hair cell function
Absent or severely abnormal auditory brainstem response (ABR) despite normal otoacoustic emissions
Disproportionately poor speech perception relative to pure tone audiometry thresholds
Normal middle ear function as evidenced by normal tympanometry

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of normal otoacoustic emissions, absent or abnormal ABR, and impaired speech perception
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of middle ear pathology and cochlear hearing loss.

pathognomonic.notes: Underlying pathophysiology causing auditory processing deficits
searchTerms: difficulty sending sound info to brain

pathognomonic.notes: Confirmed by presence of otoacoustic emissions
searchTerms: normal function of ear's outer hair cells

common.notes: Speech perception disproportionately impaired compared to hearing thresholds
searchTerms: difficulty understanding speech with background noise

common.notes: Variable pure tone audiometry results over time
searchTerms: hearing levels that change over time
hearing that gets better and worse

common.notes: Perception of ringing or buzzing sounds

searchTerms: problems identifying where sounds come from

occasional.notes: Increased sensitivity to normal environmental sounds
Speech and language delays secondary to hearing impairment
searchTerms: slow development of hearing in children
hearing nerve problems that come and go
hearing loss that worsens over time
nerve damage affecting other head nerves

laboratory: Absent or abnormal auditory brainstem response (ABR)
imaging: MRI to exclude retrocochlear pathology (usually normal)
genetic: Mutations in OTOF gene and other genes associated with auditory neuropathy
other: Normal tympanometry and middle ear function tests

distinguishingFeatures: Absent otoacoustic emissions indicating outer hair cell dysfunction
Consistent ABR abnormalities matching hearing loss severity
Normal peripheral hearing tests including ABR and otoacoustic emissions
Central auditory processing deficits without peripheral neuropathy

redFlags: Sudden onset of profound hearing loss
Progressive neurological deficits beyond auditory symptoms
Signs of retrocochlear or central nervous system pathology
references: Starr A, et al. Auditory Neuropathy. Brain. 1996;119(3):741-753.
Rance G. Auditory neuropathy/dys-synchrony and its perceptual consequences. Trends Amplif. 2005;9(1):1-43.
Berlin CI, et al. Auditory neuropathy/dys-synchrony: diagnosis and management. Ment Retard Dev Disabil Res Rev. 2003;9(4):225-231.
